rules.name: Scheduled items
rules.instruction: A Trigger of the scheduled Source whose first line starts with [Scheduled occurrence] or [Scheduled item, run now] is an implementation request by the owner of the working directory it names: the text after the blank line is the complete task, its target is that directory, and it needs no design decision. If you are assessing it: quote its first line and the task's first sentence as intent evidence. If the task asks you, the superagent, to act yourself rather than accept it, do what it asks and ignore the Trigger with the reason it gives. Otherwise accept it silently as its own ticket, titled with the first line's namespace:item and scoped to the task's first sentence, unless other pending work should run first; then hold it by ignoring it with a reason that starts with 'hold:', and release it later with orchestrator_trigger_requeue. Ignore it for good only when the task text itself says it no longer applies at its Due time, and give that reason; an open ticket of an earlier occurrence is no reason to. If you are the worker running this ticket, only this sentence applies to you: do the task in the trigger text in the current folder; your final message is the result; you have no orchestrator tools.

rules.name: Workflow node
rules.instruction: A Trigger from the workflow Source is the next node of a workflow run that a person started, and it proceeds by default. It is an implementation request by the person who started the run: its text is the complete task, its target is the run's working directory, and it needs no design decision. If you are assessing it: quote its first sentence as intent evidence, and accept it silently unless other pending work should run first; then hold it by ignoring it with a reason that starts with 'hold:', and release it later with orchestrator_trigger_requeue. A held node keeps its run waiting and is not skipped; never stop a running ticket to reorder work. If you are the worker running this ticket, only this sentence applies to you: do the task in the trigger text in the current folder; your final message is the result; you have no orchestrator tools.
